# Shutdown and Trade Risk

**Summary.** Our season ends on 2027-03-28, so March rest and shutdowns land right on playoff weeks 19 to 21. Trades must be done by 2027-03-04, about three weeks before that. Pay a little less for veterans on Golden State's gap-year roster and on teams that do not own their pick (Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans, Mavericks), and treat trade candidates as risks to their role. Keep FAB and weekly adds free for the young players who move up when a veteran is traded or rested.

## Why March matters more for us

Our playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21, and the season ends on 2027-03-28. Late-season rest and shutdowns therefore land on the weeks that decide the title. A player who rests in March costs you more than his season totals suggest. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))

Once a team decides to tank, it may shut down an injured player for the rest of the season, even if he could have come back. If a player on a losing team gets hurt in February or March, do not count on him for the playoffs. Move him to IL and replace him from waivers. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890))

The trade deadline is 2027-03-04, which also limits our own trades. Any trade happens before the playoffs, so a new role is already settled when week 19 starts. The risk is a veteran losing usage on a new team, not a surprise in the middle of the playoffs. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397))

For stars on bad teams, value a range that includes rest risk, not just per-game value. In the auction, bid on per-game value minus a discount for missed March games. Do not pay what a healthy full season would be worth. ([09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372))

## Teams to watch in March

Five teams do not control their own draft pick: the Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks. They have no reason to tank and no reason to push for wins. They may rest players, play it safe with injuries, or give young players more minutes late in the season. The notes name Brooklyn and Milwaukee as the main examples. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127))

Brooklyn is the clearest case in our player data. Julius Randle may sit some March games so the young players get time. Michael Porter Jr.'s March minutes are uncertain, and Moritz Wagner could lose minutes to the young players. Expect fewer games from Nets veterans in weeks 19 to 21. ([Julius Randle](../profiles/players/julius-randle.md), [Michael Porter Jr.](../profiles/players/michael-porter.md), [Moritz Wagner](../profiles/players/moritz-wagner.md), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))

Golden State is not on the no-pick list, but its veterans carry gap-year tags. The team is watching its lottery odds and may rest veterans. That covers Stephen Curry, Kristaps Porziņģis, Jimmy Butler III, Draymond Green, Al Horford and De'Anthony Melton. ([Stephen Curry](../profiles/players/stephen-curry.md), [Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md), [Jimmy Butler III](../profiles/players/jimmy-butler.md), [Draymond Green](../profiles/players/draymond-green.md), [Al Horford](../profiles/players/al-horford.md), [De'Anthony Melton](../profiles/players/deanthony-melton.md), [09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372))

Milwaukee, Dallas and New Orleans players in our data mostly carry trade tags, not shutdown tags. Still, the no-pick rule means rest is possible for them in March too. Kyrie Irving matters most here. How Dallas handles his back-to-backs and minutes decides how many games he plays in the 4-4-4 playoff weeks. ([Kyrie Irving](../profiles/players/kyrie-irving.md), [08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333))

## Who matters most for weeks 19 to 21

Stephen Curry is the biggest shutdown risk among players you would pay real money for. The newest expert call ranks him 12th to 13th per game but only 20th to 30th overall, because of his knee, his age and the gap-year risk. Bid up to about 30 USD and no higher. In February, check whether Golden State is resting veterans. If it is, trade him before 2027-03-04 for a player on a team still playing for something. ([Stephen Curry](../profiles/players/stephen-curry.md), [09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372))

Randle and Porter are mid-priced starters with a March problem. Draft them for the regular season at their fair prices. Before the deadline, look for a trade if you are a likely playoff team. Porter also has trade risk, since he has no extension and a trade could cut his usage further. ([Julius Randle](../profiles/players/julius-randle.md), [Michael Porter Jr.](../profiles/players/michael-porter.md), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333))

Some risks are about the schedule or a late return, not rest. Rudy Gobert has a two-game week in playoff week 20, so plan a streamer for that week. Mark Williams is expected back around mid to late March, so at best he plays part of our playoffs. Do not draft him. Watch his rehab news and the deadline. ([Rudy Gobert](../profiles/players/rudy-gobert.md), [Mark Williams](../profiles/players/mark-williams.md))

Cheap Golden State veterans are not worth an auction pick at shutdown risk, apart from IL stashes. Porziņģis is a fine 1 to 3 USD flyer for an IL slot. Butler only makes sense as a 1 USD IL stash or a waiver add when he is close to returning. Leave Green, Horford and Melton for waivers. ([Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md), [Jimmy Butler III](../profiles/players/jimmy-butler.md), [Draymond Green](../profiles/players/draymond-green.md), [Al Horford](../profiles/players/al-horford.md), [De'Anthony Melton](../profiles/players/deanthony-melton.md))

## Trade candidates and how a move changes value

Projections assume trade candidates stay with their team all season. So treat a trade as a role risk, not as built-in value. The players with the biggest auction prices and trade tags are Anthony Davis, Jamal Murray, Austin Reaves, Trey Murphy III, Domantas Sabonis and Kyrie Irving. Buy them at their fair prices and do not pay extra for trade upside. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397), [Anthony Davis](../profiles/players/anthony-davis.md), [Jamal Murray](../profiles/players/jamal-murray.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md), [Trey Murphy III](../profiles/players/trey-murphy.md), [Domantas Sabonis](../profiles/players/domantas-sabonis.md), [Kyrie Irving](../profiles/players/kyrie-irving.md))

Some trades would clearly hurt. Sabonis could end up as a backup on a contender. Norman Powell's value collapses if he becomes a third option. A trade could cut Porter's usage further. A Denver deal could shrink Cameron Johnson's role. For these players, follow trade news closely in late February. Be ready to sell before 2027-03-04 if a deal looks likely. ([Domantas Sabonis](../profiles/players/domantas-sabonis.md), [Norman Powell](../profiles/players/norman-powell.md), [Michael Porter Jr.](../profiles/players/michael-porter.md), [Cameron Johnson](../profiles/players/cameron-johnson.md))

For some players, a trade could go either way. Zach LaVine's role could rise or fall after a trade, buyout or minutes cut. Murray faces a possible salary dump. Davis has Golden State rumors, and he would join a team talking about a gap year. Check each player's new team and minutes in the first week after a deal before you start him in the playoffs. ([Zach LaVine](../profiles/players/zach-lavine.md), [Jamal Murray](../profiles/players/jamal-murray.md), [Anthony Davis](../profiles/players/anthony-davis.md))

Most late-auction trade candidates are cheap, so the risk is small: Jalen Suggs, Daniel Gafford, RJ Barrett, Aaron Gordon, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Jerami Grant and Christian Braun. Spend 1 USD on them at most and drop them if a trade costs them minutes. ([Jalen Suggs](../profiles/players/jalen-suggs.md), [Daniel Gafford](../profiles/players/daniel-gafford.md), [RJ Barrett](../profiles/players/rj-barrett.md), [Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md), [Jaime Jaquez Jr.](../profiles/players/jaime-jaquez.md), [Jerami Grant](../profiles/players/jerami-grant.md), [Christian Braun](../profiles/players/christian-braun.md))

## Young players who can gain

Projections that keep trade candidates on their teams can understate the young players behind them. Teams with nothing to play for in March can also move minutes to young players. Save part of your FAB and your 6 weekly adds for the days after 2027-03-04 and the first weeks of March. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127))

Specific links from the notes: Burries is Milwaukee's long-term shooting guard if Tyler Herro's expiring deal is moved. Anthony Black becomes startable if Orlando trades Suggs or Suggs gets hurt. Leonard Miller is the reason Jalen Smith could be moved. Maluach would keep the job ahead of Mark Williams. In Atlanta, Daniels could make Luguentz Dort expendable. ([Tyler Herro](../profiles/players/tyler-herro.md), [Anthony Black](../profiles/players/anthony-black.md), [Jalen Suggs](../profiles/players/jalen-suggs.md), [Jalen Smith](../profiles/players/jalen-smith.md), [Mark Williams](../profiles/players/mark-williams.md), [Luguentz Dort](../profiles/players/luguentz-dort.md))

Ryan Rollins is the clearest young beneficiary you can draft. He shares Milwaukee's crowded backcourt with Herro, so a Herro trade should help his usage. He also carries his own trade risk as a cheap contract Milwaukee could flip for picks. A LaVine trade or injury could also open backup guard minutes for Malik Monk in Sacramento. Watch Monk on waivers, not in the auction. ([Ryan Rollins](../profiles/players/ryan-rollins.md), [Tyler Herro](../profiles/players/tyler-herro.md), [Malik Monk](../profiles/players/malik-monk.md), [Zach LaVine](../profiles/players/zach-lavine.md))

Where the sources differ: the method notes agree that no-pick teams may rest veterans. They differ on the reason. One note says these teams have no reason to tank and no downside either. Another says they may still lean on young players and protect injured ones. Prices differ more. Our league paid 42 USD for Curry last season, while the experts now rank him 20th to 30th overall. The ESPN value of Davis assumes a healthy season, while the expert round 3 range does not. Bid at the risk-adjusted expert range, not the healthy-season value. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127), [Stephen Curry](../profiles/players/stephen-curry.md), [Anthony Davis](../profiles/players/anthony-davis.md))
